title: E-Learning Course on Sleep for Parents of Premature Infants
summary:
In the first few months of life, a baby's sleep patterns change dramatically. Approximately a quarter of babies experience problems such as difficulty falling asleep or frequent awakenings during the night. Premature babies, in particular, are more prone to sleep problems – which can be stressful for the whole family. 
This pilot study will test a sleep-related e-learning program for parents of premature babies. The program will explain why sleep is important for premature babies, how their sleep develops, and what special considerations to expect.
A total of 60 people will participate in the study, divided into two groups.
Group 1: 30 participants will complete questionnaires about their own sleep quality. After three months, we will contact these parents again via email and send them a link to three questionnaires: one about their own sleep quality, one about their child's sleep, and one about their sense of parental competence regarding sleep.
Group 2: We ask 30 people to participate in a sleep-related e-learning course and afterwards to complete a feedback form and a questionnaire about their own sleep quality. After three months, we contact these parents again by email and send them three further questionnaires: another questionnaire about their own sleep quality, a questionnaire about their child's sleep, and one about their sense of competence as parents regarding sleep.

interventions.name: Thirty participants (caregivers of premature infants) will be asked to answer questions about their demographics and their own sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI) at two time points (shortly before discharge from the neonatal unit and after three months). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Parent or guardian of a prematurely born child (born at fewer than 37 weeks gestational age)
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of access to an internet-enabled device; insufficient German language skills.
